thread:
Iris: Dropping a quick convo about the usage & billing panel. Idea: a small floating action area on the chart (bottom-right) that exposes exports + scope summary on hover, instead of cramming everything into the top bar. Pros: keeps header light, actions are contextual. Cons: discoverability? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/new-floating (page 'Floating Export CTA').

Tom: Interesting. Floating CTA could work as long as it has a visible affordance on first load (badge or pulse). My worry: keyboard users might miss it if it's out of tab order. If we do this, it must be focusable and included in the logical DOM flow.

Hannah: From a UX POV, users expect scope controls near filters. If export is floating, show a tiny label on the left of the chart: "Scope: Org / Project" + chevron to open scope settings. Floating CTA then only handles export formats. That splits concerns nicely.

Iris: Good split. For export wording, how about "Export billing (CSV)" as primary and menu options: "CSV (rollup)", "CSV (per-project, zipped)", "PDF (queued)"? Show ETA on PDF. Default click = start CSV download and show toast with link.

Tom: Perf note: per-project CSV should stream. Backend can return a pre-signed URL and a request_id header. Also add a small progress indicator in the toast if it's a zip.

Hannah: Labeling: change token label from "Tokens" to "Token units (in + out)" and show inline example: "e.g., prompt 20, completion 80 = 100 tokens". Small question-mark links to docs. This helps support tickets.

Iris: A11y: must ensure floating CTA is in tab order and announces scope/date when menu opens. Also add aria-live region for export completion notifications. @a11y-bot can you run checks on the pattern?

dev-bot: created preview build for feature/floating-export (build #821)  https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/821

a11y-bot: queued scan for feature/floating-export. Quick findings: floating CTA not reachable by keyboard in current prototype; menu missing aria-haspopup; export toast not aria-live. Contrast OK. Full report: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/821

Tom: Implementation plan: 1) keep scope chips near top-left (filters), 2) floating export CTA bottom-right (focusable + visible badge on first visit), 3) default CSV with caret menu, PDF w/ ETA, per-project zipped option, 4) telemetry for export.format and scope.context. Owners: Hannah (copy + first-visit badge), Iris (design + figma update), Tom (backend + toast).

Hannah: I'll add the token explainer copy and the first-visit tooltip. Also will add microcopy for the per-project zip: "Per-project CSV (zipped) 4 may take several minutes".

Iris: I'll update Figma and add keyboard demo frames showing tab -> open menu -> choose format with Enter. Will also add a11y notes in the file.

Tom: I'll wire up streaming endpoints and ensure response headers include request_id and pricing_version. Also will add telemetry to the export flow.

a11y-bot: re-run scheduled after updates. New scan: floating CTA is keyboard reachable, menu has aria attributes, toast announces via aria-live="polite". Two remaining issues: chart SVG needs <desc> and per-point aria-labels for screen readers. Report: https://ci.redwood.ai/a11y/821-2

Iris: Great progress. We'll validate in tomorrow's usability pass. Thanks! :sparkles:
